title: Finite normal model over a finite part of a perfect closure
statement: Let k and K be fields [def-weil-field], with K/k a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is perfect and purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and let q:X to Spec k be a finite type morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There is a finite intermediate field E of K/k, a scheme Y with a finite surjective morphism f:Y to X_E [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and a dense open U of X_E such that f inverse U is dense in Y and f restricted to U is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Every stalk of Y_K is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here Y_K is the base change of f followed by the projection X_E to Spec E along E to K. This asserts a finite model with a dense closed-immersion locus, without identifying it with normalization at the finite stage or asserting normality over every field extension of E.

source.place: Tag 0BXT, proof through the descent of the dense open and its closed immersion; Limits Tags 01ZM, 01ZO, 01Z4, 01ZP

proof.text: Use the algebraicity instance of the purely inseparable extension and the existing subextSpecCone/isLimitSubextSpecCone to express Spec K as the limit of spectra of finite intermediate fields. Base-change this cone along q, after identifying k with the bottom intermediate field, using baseChangeDiagram, baseChangeCone and isLimitBaseChangeCone. Stages are qcqs because X is finite type over a field and transitions are affine.

Let T be this limit base change, R its reduction and r:R to T the reduction map. The reduction theorem makes r a surjective closed immersion and a homeomorphism. Apply reduced_algebraic_normalization_field_change to R over K. Its componentwise normalization N has a finite surjective map to R, normal domain stalks, and is an isomorphism over a dense open V of R. Compose with r to get a finite surjective map nu:N to T. Let W=r(V), an open because r is a homeomorphism. Its preimage under r is V. Thus W is dense, nu inverse W is dense by dense_preimage_normalization, and the restriction of nu to W is a closed immersion (an isomorphism followed by the restricted reduction).

The finite morphism nu to the Noetherian scheme T is locally of finite presentation (IsFinite.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isLocallyNoetherian), quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation to descend it to a finite-presentation stage model. Descend the compact open W by exists_preimage_eq; compactness follows from Noetherianity. Cofilteredness gives a common stage for the model and the open, and base-change pasting supplies its Cartesian comparison.

The comparison T to X_E is a base change of Spec K to Spec E, so is faithfully flat, surjective and quasi-compact. Descend finiteness directly by the source-library fpqc finiteness theorem. Restrict the Cartesian square to the descended open and descend the closed immersion by its fpqc descent theorem. This avoids the two general eventual-stage descent lemmas: field extensions are already faithfully flat at the selected stage. In Lean the field-spectrum fpqc conjunction comes from fpqcCover_specMap_algebraMap_of_field; the private restriction-square helper is proved by pasting the canonical restriction squares (the elementary proof of source GenericModelAux, without importing its unrelated generic-smoothness theory).

Surjectivity of the finite-stage model follows by lifting a target point to T, lifting that point along nu, and mapping it to the model. Density of the descended open is reflected along the surjective continuous comparison: the image of its dense preimage is dense and contained in the open. The same argument on N to the model proves density of the inverse image. The latter map is surjective by base change. Identify the selected stage with the literal pullback X_E using the bottom-field isomorphism. Paste the Cartesian comparisons to identify N with the specified K-base change of Y. Isomorphisms induce stalk ring isomorphisms, transporting the normal domain stalks of N to that base change. The chosen E is finite by its index; no nonempty-scheme hypothesis is used, so the empty case is included.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_perfectClosure_finite_normal_model
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [IsPurelyInseparable k K] [PerfectField K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (q : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [QuasiCompact q] :
    ∃ E : IntermediateField k K, Module.Finite k E ∧
      ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u})
        (f : Y ⟶ pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
        (U : (pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E)))).Opens),
        IsFinite f ∧ Surjective f ∧
        Dense (Set.range U.ι) ∧
        Dense (f ⁻¹ᵁ U : Set Y) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (f ∣_ U) ∧
        ∀ z : (pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K))) : Scheme.{u}),
          IsDomain ((pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K)))).presheaf.stalk z) ∧
          IsIntegrallyClosed ((pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K)))).presheaf.stalk z)
